\caption{Do two leave-one-out contributions add? Each panel holds the complete solver, the two single-mechanism removals, and the cell with both removed --- same instances, same seeds, same move budget. $\Delta$ is the median soft cost against the complete solver at that size. The interaction contrast is per seed, $I = (\textrm{both} - \textrm{no chain}) - (\textrm{no swap} - \textrm{full})$, expressed as a share of that seed's own complete-solver cost; it is zero when the two losses add. Each panel's medians are taken over the seeds \emph{this} cell carries, which is more than the leave-one-out batch received, so a configuration's entry here may differ by a few tenths of a point from the same configuration in Table~\ref{tab:ablation-moves}; the two are the same experiment on different sample sizes and neither is a correction of the other. An exact two-sided signed-rank test cannot report a $p$ below $2/2^{k}$ on $k$ paired seeds --- $10$ seeds at $n = 3\,200$ put its floor at $p = 0.002$, and $10$ seeds at $n = 12\,800$ put its floor at $p = 0.002$ --- so the test is reported as a consistency check and never as the basis of a claim, and the per-seed contrasts are given in full so that a reader can judge the spread directly.}
